per_question.question: How long should I wait after isolating an inverter before opening the cabinet?
per_question.answer: Each Authorised Person attaches a personal lock and a tag showing name, date and PTW number to every isolation point [1]. Wait at least 10 minutes after isolation before opening converter or inverter cabinets, so the DC-link capacitors can discharge [1].

per_question.question: Who can remove someone else's lock if that person has gone home?
per_question.answer: Only the person who applied a lock may remove it [1]. If that person is unavailable, the Shift In-charge may authorise removal only after 3 documented attempts to contact them and with written approval from the Site Manager [1]. The incoming Authorised Person applies their own lock before the outgoing person removes theirs [2].

per_question.question: What wind speed is too high to climb a turbine tower?
per_question.answer: Tower climbing is permitted only when the 10-minute average wind speed is below 18 m/s [1]. Work in the hub or on the blades requires the 10-minute average wind speed to be below 12 m/s [1].

per_question.question: Is lightning a reason to stop climbing, and how long do we wait before resuming?
per_question.answer: Work in the hub or on the blades requires the 10-minute average wind speed to be below 12 m/s [1]. If lightning is detected within 10 km of the site, stop all climbing and wait 30 minutes after the last strike before resuming [1].

per_question.question: How often does a climbing harness need a certified inspection?
per_question.answer: Inspect the harness before every use [1]. Harnesses also need a certified inspection once a year [1]. Damaged equipment must be tagged out and removed from service [1].

per_question.question: At what oil temperature does the gearbox trip?
per_question.answer: Oil sump temperature: raise a warning at 75 degrees C and the turbine trips at 85 degrees C [4]. Filter differential pressure of 2.5 bar or more means the filter must be replaced [4].

per_question.question: How frequently should gearbox oil samples be sent to the lab?
per_question.answer: Check the oil level at the sight glass during every quarterly service [1]. Take an oil sample every 6 months for laboratory analysis [1]. Inspect the oil filter at each quarterly service [1]. This procedure covers oil sampling, level checks and condition monitoring of the main gearbox [2].

per_question.question: What should we do if the gearbox oil shows high water content?
per_question.answer: Oil sump temperature: raise a warning at 75 degrees C and the turbine trips at 85 degrees C [1]. Filter differential pressure of 2.5 bar or more means the filter must be replaced [1]. A water content above 500 ppm requires a work order for a moisture investigation [1]. The target particle cleanliness is ISO 4406 18/16/13 [1].

per_question.question: How do I handle inverter fault E-204?
per_question.answer: Isolate the inverter on both AC and DC sides and apply LOTO [1]. Disconnect each DC string one by one [1]. Measure the insulation resistance of each string with a 1000 V megger [1]. A string reading below 1 megohm is faulty [1]. Mark it and raise a work order for the cable or module [1]. Restart the inverter only after all strings pass the test [1].

per_question.question: When should solar PV modules be cleaned?
per_question.answer: Clean the modules when the soiling loss exceeds 4 percent [1]. Use dry brushing or demineralised water only [1].

per_question.question: A Buchholz relay alarm came on. Can we re-energise the transformer?
per_question.answer: A Buchholz relay alarm must be treated as a possible internal fault [1]. Do not re-energise the transformer until dissolved gas analysis (DGA) of the oil has been completed and reviewed by the Substation Engineer [1].

per_question.question: What earth resistance is acceptable for the switchyard?
per_question.answer: Replace the silica gel breather when more than two-thirds of the gel has changed colour from blue to pink [1]. Test switchyard earth resistance once a year [1]. The value must be below 1 ohm [1].

per_question.question: What are the transformer top-oil alarm and trip temperatures?
per_question.answer: Top-oil temperature: alarm at 85 degrees C and trip at 95 degrees C [1]. Winding temperature: alarm at 95 degrees C and trip at 105 degrees C [1].

per_question.question: Within how long must a serious S1 incident be reported to the Regional Head?
per_question.answer: For S1, notify the Site Manager immediately and the Regional Head within 1 hour [1]. Submit a written preliminary report within 24 hours [1].

per_question.question: Who contacts the regulator after an incident?
per_question.answer: Notifications to external authorities and regulators are made only by the Compliance team [1]. Site staff must not contact regulators directly [1].

per_question.question: What cell temperature triggers the stage 2 alarm in a battery container?
per_question.answer: Operators must start monitoring and reduce power [1]. Stage 2 alarm: any cell temperature above 70 degrees C [1]. The battery management system isolates the rack and the HVAC runs at maximum [1].

per_question.question: How far away should people muster during a BESS thermal event?
per_question.answer: Raise the emergency alarm and inform the control room [2]. Evacuate all personnel to the muster point at least 50 m upwind of the container [2]. Do not open the container doors [2].

per_question.question: At what wind speed do turbines cut out automatically?
per_question.answer: Turbines shut down automatically at a cut-out wind speed of 25 m/s, measured as a 10-minute average [1]. A turbine may restart only when the average wind speed stays below 20 m/s for 10 minutes [1].

per_question.question: What must be true before restarting turbines after a grid outage?
per_question.answer: After a grid outage, do not restart turbines or inverters until the grid voltage and frequency are stable [1]. Wait 5 minutes of stable supply with frequency between 49.5 and 50.5 Hz [1]. Restart units in stages, not all at once, to avoid a sudden power surge [1].

per_question.question: When do solar trackers go to stow position?
per_question.answer: Move single-axis trackers to the stow position when the wind speed exceeds 15 m/s [1]. Resume normal tracking when the wind stays below 12 m/s for 15 minutes [1].

per_question.question: What torque should I use on the inverter DC terminals?
per_question.answer: Flag any connector that is more than 20 degrees C hotter than the adjacent connectors [1]. Terminal torque must follow the OEM datasheet [1]. This procedure does not specify torque values [1].

per_question.question: What happens to the locks at shift handover?
per_question.answer: Locks stay in place across shift changes [1]. The incoming Authorised Person applies their own lock before the outgoing person removes theirs [1]. The LOTO register must be updated at every handover [1].

per_question.question: How is a near miss classified and when is it logged?
per_question.answer: S2: lost-time injury or equipment damage above INR 10 lakh [1]. S3: first-aid case or near miss with no injury [1].

per_question.question: What protective equipment is mandatory for tower climbing?
per_question.answer: Wear a full-body harness with dual lanyards and maintain 100% tie-off at all times [1]. A helmet with chin strap, safety shoes and gloves are mandatory [1]. Inspect the harness before every use [1].
